Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Work & responsibility

professional noun and adjective

someone who does it for a living, not as an amateur

also a professional, turn professional, pro, expert, amateur

classical

Cic. Mur. 29: in Graecīs artificibus
M-O s.v. professional photographer (Egger)

artifex, artificis m.

noun, third declension

a professional, a master of an art

The practitioner as against the layman, idiōta (Cic. Verr. 2.4.4: quōs iste idiōtās appellat); artificēs scaenicī are professional performers (Cic. Arch. 10, Lewis & Short). For “professional” meaning “to do with one’s work”, Latin uses the noun: ars, artificium.

Examples

  • Ut ajunt in Graecīs artificibus eōs auloedōs esse quī citharoedī fierī nōn potuerint

    As they say of Greek professional musicians, that those who could not become lyre-singers become pipe-singersCic. Mur. 29

Other words

  • perītus, perīta, perītum — expert, skilled (with the genitive)

    adjective · also used · classical · M-O s.v. expert: (homō) perītus; Cic. Imp. Pomp. 68: bellōrum omnium perītissimus (Lewis & Short)

See also trade, career, experience.

SourcesLewis & Short: artifex · Lewis & Short: idiota · Lewis & Short: peritus

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. professional photographer; expert.

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
